data.name: ALONE?
data.detailed_description:
A Psychological Horror Game About Family.

THE GAME

Explore and experience a fully immersive world as you embark on an ghostly adventure unlike anything you have played before. Come face-to-face with terror itself as you navigate around a haunted house, underground caverns, caves, and an old decrepit morgue. But beware: some mysteries are better left alone.

SYNOPSIS

Your sister Michelle, is missing. All you have to go by is a letter that was sent to you by post. The letter is a plea for help; it begs for you to return to the home you grew up in, and to save her from the strange occurrences that have been plaguing her over the past few months.

THE FIRST 5 MINUTES OF THE GAME

When you begin, you have entered your sister’s house. Rain pours down from the heavens and distant sounds of thunder and lightning can be heard. You struggle to breathe as you take your first step forward in to the darkness. Brace yourself, things are not what they seem.

FEATURES


  • A UNIQUE HORROR EXPERIENCE: Designed to provide a psychological horror experience. The game will consistently aim to unnerve the player, and will change the landscape and direction as you play. Nothing is as it seems, and nothing can be trusted.
  • INTERACTION: The game features true immersion by allowing you to interact with around 80% of the items in game.
  • JUMP SCARES AND FRIGHTS: Scares await you in this haunted location. You have been warned.
  • DYNAMIC CHANGING WORLD: As you move around the world, paranormal events happen consistently. Brace yourself for anything to happen, and at any time.
  • ATMOSPHERIC SOUND: Provides a perfect soundtrack which enhances game-play, immersion and tension.
  • MULTIPLE ENDINGS: A tense story with 4 endings, that leaves you yearning to explore every nook and cranny.
  • GRAPHICS: Designed to run at 60 fps at 1920x1080 on most PCs.

Note: This is a horror game, and as such, persons suffering a weak heart may be effected.

reviews.review:
[h1]Overview:[/h1]
'[i]ALONE?[/i]' is a short first person walking simulator in the horror genre following a troubled man searching for his sister "Michelle" after initially receiving a concerning letter of distress, urging him to return home. The game is rather short albeit with multiple endings each obtainable based on the decisions you make in the game. You may think that means there's replay value here but there really isn't. They're all underwhelming and one of them is literally just you leaving the house the second you enter to building. As a whole, '[i]ALONE?[/i]' isn't a [i]horrible[/i] game by any stretch but it definitely has it's issues. Clunky controls, slow pacing along with some corny jumpscares are only a few pet peeves I have with the game.

[h1]Gameplay:[/h1]
'[i]ALONE?[/i]' plays like your standard first person walking simulator with your run-of-the-mill jumpscares. You explore multiple different environments with various forks that you can take which can ultimately change the ending of the game. The environments I [i]will[/i] say are pretty good when it comes to the ambience and atmospheric horror. Many things can be interacted with which gives the game a big sense of immersion as you never really feel like you're just walking through a canvas.

The protagonist will make comments on the smallest most inconvenient things which to some people can offer a bit of background storytelling which can be nice. I can safely say I was pretty on my toes plaything through the game, knowing that jumpscares would be inbound. The jumpscares themselves are cheap and pretty corny with some not being all that scary. They're typically where you'd expect them to be but many of them are only scary cause the noise that plays when they trigger startle you more than anything.

Aside from the setting and atmosphere, the horror element is pretty lacking. The game kind of kept me on my toes mainly cause my mindset hovered around the idea of jumpscares triggering when I interacted with objects which is standard for most horror games and considering how many things you can interact with, I was pretty paranoid. Also, the game has a background ambience that contains some sound effects that threw me off despite it not actually contributing to anything happening in the game such as a door creaking and footsteps in the distance.

The main other gripe I have with the game is the somewhat awkward and inconsistent controls that come with it. I'm not sure exactly what it is but the mouse controls are weird and choppy when looking around. The mouse sensitivity is all over the place and feels restricted. It's very uncomfortable to play and that's on top of the slow paced movement with even the sprint function feeling non-existent. There were times I couldn't interact with certain things unless looking at it from a specific angle or fidgeting around with it. It just made playing the game feel weird as if I didn't have full control over what I was doing. If you can somehow look passed this flaw and adapt to it, then maybe you could find some enjoyment out of this game but it isn't easy.

[h1]Controls:[/h1]
As mentioned the mouse movement is questionable and affects the gameplay in a negative way. It can be annoying trying to play the game when looking around and interacting with things can be tedious at times. There are a handful of things such as drawers and cupboards that open when interacting with them but they do so slowly and you're stuck waiting for them every time. It eventually becomes annoying cause you wish you could just move as they're opening instead of having to watch them every single time.

The settings menu is also finicky and there were times I found myself stuck in it after adjusting some settings cause it wouldn't close. The mouse sensitivity option is barely useable as adjusting it even slightly can greatly impact how your mouse moves around meaning there's only one small area that's useable. Maxing it out makes the protagonist look around as if they're having a seizure and lowering it fully makes you unable to look around altogether. The game overall just feels sloppy and unpolished. There's even a "Field of View" option that still says "(in development)" and the game is almost 10 years old.

[h1]Graphics:[/h1]
Not very good. The game looks flat despite the rooms having a decent amount of clutter in them. Much of this may have to do with the shaders feeling more static than dynamic. The colors are drab and the world feels dated with pale colors plastered around the game at every turn. There aren't any graphics settings either aside from resolution which is just scaling and gamma which is just brightness. The only other thing is field of view which as I mentioned, is "still in development" which I put in quotes cause it clearly isn't.

[h1]Audio:[/h1]
This is kind of okay, the ambience is pretty decent but I could've done without the deceptive sound effects that accompanied it. On top of that, the ambience still made the game feel quiet, keeping me on guard pretty much all throughout my playthroughs. The jumpscare noises however are pretty cheesy. It did get a me a few times but the aftermath was more laughing at the silliness of them as opposed to actual appreciation of a good scare.

[h1]Conclusion/TL;DR:[/h1]
'[i]ALONE?[/i]' is a short, unpolished first person horror walking simulator where you play as a man returning home after receiving a cry for help from his sister. The game has a decent atmosphere of suspense but is plagued with issues ranging from cheap, underwhelming jumpscares, rough programming and a mouse movement system so flawed it's made the game unplayable to a handful of users. It's a game that although can be played to those who can adapt to it's flawed design, isn't really worth it for the content that it offers.
